rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in “upon it” refers to the earth, either by proximity or directly to the earlier mention of Earth.
rows.anchor: Bu عَلَيْهَا zamiri cevârî dolayısıyla yahut doğrudan doğru yukarıdaki “Arz”a râci‘dir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone on earth perishes, including those aboard ships as well as everyone else.
rows.anchor: Yani o Arz üzerinde bulunan her kim olursa olsun hepsi fânîdir. Gerek o gemilerdekiler, gerek diğerleri hepsi de

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the enduring face of the Lord to mean God’s Essence, as in 28:88; the grammatical agreement that follows supports this reading.
rows.anchor: “vech” كُلُّ شَىْءٍ هَالِكٌ إِلَّا وَجْهَهُۥ’de [el-Kasas 28/88] olduğu gibi Zât-ı Rab mânasına olduğu anlaşılıyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative “Dhu” makes majesty and generosity an adjective of “face”; if it modified “Lord,” it would be genitive.
rows.anchor: “Zü’l-celâli ve’l-ikrâm” sıfatı “zû” diye merfu olarak “vech”e sıfat yapılmıştır. Eğer öyle olmasa idi

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Baydawi glosses the face as the Essence, while also allowing it to mean the direction toward God or a direction He possesses.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî “Zât” ile tefsir ettikten sonra şöyle demiştir: “Mevcûdâtın cihetlerini istikrâ

rows.speaker: Şihâb
rows.claim: Shihab calls this an alternative exegesis: “face” means the direction toward which one aims, not a metaphor for the Essence.
rows.anchor: Hâşiyesinde Şihâb bunu şöyle îzah etmiştir: “Bu diğer bir tefsirdir.

rows.speaker: Makdisî
rows.claim: Makdisi says contingent things are inherently liable to nonexistence; only the side God turns toward and grants existence is excepted.
rows.anchor: Üstadımız Makdisî kaddesallahu rûhahu dedi ki: ‘Haddizâtında adem olanda asıl, kendi zatı itibariyle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God’s regard and bestowal of existence, contingent things would have no existence and remain absent.
rows.anchor: Hakk’ın ona nazarı ve hil‘at-i vücûdu ifazası olmasa idi onun için vücud şerefi hâsıl olmazdı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes take “face” to mean righteous deeds done to draw near to God.
rows.anchor: Şu hâlde bazı tefsirlerde olduğu gibi “vech” ile amel-i sâlih murad olunmak da mümkin olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A righteous deed is kept for its doer until God rewards it, so its reward remains in place of the deed.
rows.anchor: abd, onu emre imtisâlen işleyince Allah ona mükâfâtını verinceye kadar onu onun için ibkā eder.

rows.speaker: Meşâyıhımızdan bazısı
rows.claim: Some of the author’s shaykhs identify the imperishable face with God’s sustaining care of created things, an attribute of the divine Essence.
rows.anchor: Meşâyıhımızdan bazısı da şöyle dedi: O adem-i fenâ ile mevsuf olan vech, Allah teâlâ’nın mevcûdâta kayyûmiyetidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Salaf approach, affirm the reported attributes such as face and hand without asking how they are or interpreting them.
rows.anchor: Selef mezhebince giderek vech, yed gibi sıfatları isbat eder

rows.speaker: Muhakkikler
rows.claim: The realized knowers refuse to witness anything besides God because they recognize His sustaining and abiding encompassment of all things.
rows.anchor: bazı ârifler demişlerdir ki muhakkikler Allah teâlâ’nın gayrısına şehadetten ibâ ettiler. Çünkü O, onları şuhûd-ı kayyûmiyyet

rows.speaker: İbn Atâ
rows.claim: Ibn Ata says created existence is darkness, illuminated only by God’s manifestation; whoever sees creation without witnessing God in, before, after, or alongside it is veiled from the lights of knowledge.
rows.anchor: İbn Atâ demiştir ki kevn, hep zulmettir. Onu ancak Hak teâlâ’nın onda zuhûru nurlandırmaktadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although “face” can denote created beings’ God-facing relation and their benefit from divine lordship and emanation, the majesty-and-generosity epithet rules these readings out here and identifies God’s Essence.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı, Allah yüzü eşyânın veya insanların Allah’a bakan yüzü, yani kendi zatlarına nazaran değil de Allah teâlâ’nın rubûbiyetinden

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it God’s face rather than simply saying “your Lord remains” emphasizes the permanence of the Essence through the manifestation of attributes and lordship; the sustaining-attribute reading makes this point too.
rows.anchor: Bunun nüktesi Zât’ın yalnız bâtında ve mücerred zat olarak değil, sıfât[^10]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majesty signifies absolute greatness and self-sufficiency that overwhelms all; generosity gives existence and complete care even to the nonexistent and perishing.
rows.anchor: azamet ve celâli ile her şeyi kahr u ifnâ edebilecek derecede büyüklük ve istiğnâ-yı mutlak sâhibi, hem de ma‘dum ve fânîlere vücud vererek

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib says the attribute “Possessor of Majesty and Generosity” is exclusive to God and is among His most particular attributes.
rows.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “İşbu Zü’l-celâli ve’likrâm sıfatı Allah teâlâ’ya mahsus olan ve O’nun gayrısında kullanılmayan sıfatlardandır.

rows.speaker: Enes, Rebî‘a b. Âmir
rows.claim: A Prophetic report transmitted by Tirmidhi from Anas and Ahmad from Rabi'a ibn Amir urges frequent, steadfast repetition of “O Possessor of Majesty and Generosity” in supplication.
rows.anchor: Tirmizî’nin Enes’ten, İmam Ahmed’in Rebî‘a b. Âmir’den merfû‘an rivayet ettikleri şu hadîs-i şerîf de buna şehadet eder

rows.speaker: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet calls a prayer invoking God’s praise, generosity, majesty, life, and self-subsistence a supplication by the Greatest Name, which ensures a response and grants what is asked.
rows.anchor: Bunun üzerine Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem ashâbına buyurdu ki: “Biliyor musunuz ne ile dua etti?”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since you are perishable while your Lord’s generosity remains after your death, the refrain asks how you can deny His favors.
rows.anchor: Yani siz kendiniz hep fâni olduğunuz hâlde sizin fenânızdan sonra bile ikrâmı bâkī olan Rabbinizin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle “fa” links the refrain to the prior verse: perishing opens the way to permanence, eternal life, and lasting reward.
rows.anchor: Bu surette “fâ” evvelki âyetin mazmûnuna terettüb ediyor. Çünkü fenâ bekānın, ebedî hayâtın, sermedî nimet ile sevâbın bir kapısı olmuş oluyor.

rows.speaker: Tîbî
rows.claim: Tibi says the preceding verse implies the arrival of judgment and reward; warning against punishable acts is itself a favor, and the refrain invites people to value it.
rows.anchor: Tîbî[^17] demiştir ki: “Âyet-i sâbıkadan murad mânasının melzûmudur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that both God’s majesty and generosity are blessings; the question also challenges why people neither fear His majesty nor seek His generosity.
rows.anchor: Bunu şöyle de anlayabiliriz: Allah’ın celâlinde de nimet, ikrâmında da nimet vardır. Yahut şöyle diyebiliriz: Allah’ın celâlinden nasıl korkmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone in heaven and earth continually asks God for what they need in coming into being, remaining in being, and every other state, since they have no claim to existence in themselves.
rows.anchor: Göklerde ve yerde olan herkes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God continually acts in majesty or generosity, granting requests and, by His wise will, extinguishing and creating, enriching some, and changing circumstances.
rows.anchor: Hak celle ve alâ hikem-i bâliğaya mübtenî[^23] meşiyyeti muktezâsınca her lahza nicelerini ifnâ

rows.speaker: Ebu’d-Derdâ
rows.claim: The Prophet says that forgiving sins, relieving distress, raising some people and lowering others are among God’s affairs.
rows.anchor: İbn Mâce ve İbn Hibbân ve daha birtakımları Ebu’d-Derdâ radıyallâhu anh’tan rivayet etmişlerdir ki Hazret-i Peygamber sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bu âyette şöyle buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: Bezzâr
rows.claim: Al-Bazzar’s version adds that answering prayers is also among God’s affairs.
rows.anchor: Bezzâr’ın rivayetinde “dualara icâbet buyurmak” ziyâdesi de vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation takes “day” to mean any period of time, so the phrase means every hour or moment.
rows.anchor: Birisi “yevm” mutlak vakit mânasına olarak her saat her lahza mânasına tefsir edilmiştir.

rows.speaker: İbn Uyeyne, Hasan-ı Basrî
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna and Hasan al-Basri say time consists, for God, of this world and the afterlife: His affair in the world is command and prohibition, and in the afterlife reckoning and recompense.
rows.anchor: İbn Uyeyne’den ve Hasan-ı Basrî’den nakledildiği üzere Allah teâlâ’ya göre dehr iki günden ibarettir. Birisi dünya birisi âhirettir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We shall attend to you” uses metaphor or metonymy: emptying ordinarily presupposes being occupied, but nothing distracts God; the phrase means the afterlife reckoning and requital will be devoted to you.
rows.anchor: “Ferâğ” lügatta boşalmak demek olduğundan önce bir meşguliyet ister[^27]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The two weighty ones” is a title for human beings and jinn, made explicit by the following verse.
rows.anchor: “sekalân” yahut “sekaleyn”, iki sekal, bundan sonraki âyette tasrih olunacağı üzere ins ü cinnin bir unvânıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One proposed origin compares earth to a laden animal bearing humans and jinn as two heavy loads; other creatures are treated as extra additions.
rows.anchor: Arz bir yüklü hayvana ve ins ü cin ona yükletilmiş iki ağır denge benzetilerek bu isim verilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation derives the title from physical weight or the gravity of human reason and the importance of human rank on earth.
rows.anchor: Arz üzerinde ağırlıkları veya re’ylerinin rezâneti ve kadr ü şanlarının

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say humans and jinn are called “the two weighty ones” because they are burdened by religious obligation.
rows.anchor: Bundan başka teklif ile kendilerine ağırlık verilmiş olduğundan denilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another proposed reason for the title is the weight of their sins.
rows.anchor: günah ile ağırlıklarından dolayı da denilmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the Prophet left the community two weighty things: God’s Book and his family, showing that the term can refer to spiritual weight and standing.
rows.anchor: bunda “sekaleyn” tâbiri Kitâbullah gibi kadr ü şânı büyük olan mânevî ağırlıklar hakkında

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that humans and jinn be called “the two weighty ones” for their spiritual, rather than merely material, status.
rows.anchor: Yani ins ü cinne maddî haysiyetlerinden ziyade mânevî haysiyetleri itibariyle “sekalân” ıtlak edilmiş olması şâyân-ı tercih görünür.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning asks how people can deny present life’s favors or tomorrow’s punishment and reward; the warning itself is a favor, and ingratitude risks deprivation and danger.
rows.anchor: Yani yarın böyle hesâbı gelip çatacak iken gerek bugün içinde bulunduğunuz hayat nimetlerine ve gerek yarının cezâ ve mükâfâtına nasıl küfran edersiniz?

words: إِنِ ٱسْتَطَعْتُمْ أَن تَنفُذُوا۟ مِنْ أَقْطَارِ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans and jinn are challenged to escape through the bounds of heaven and earth, meaning to flee God’s dominion and sovereignty.
rows.anchor: o semâvât ve Arz’ın aktârından, göklerin ve yerin hudûd u eb‘âdından çıkıp gitmeye gücünüz yeterse

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to go forth is a taʿjiz challenge, exposing their inability to escape.
rows.anchor: kendinizi kurtarın. Bu emir ta‘cîz emridir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Authority” may mean some other force or sovereignty strong enough to overcome the powers of heaven and earth, a force humans and jinn do not possess.
rows.anchor: bir sultan olmadıkça yani bütün o göklerin ve yerin kuvvetlerini mağlub edecek başkaca bir kuvvet ve saltanat olmadıkça çıkamazsınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More precisely, escape would require power or a decree granted by God; without it they cannot flee.
rows.anchor: Daha doğrusu Allah teâlâ tarafından bahşedilecek bir kuvvet veya bir ferman olmadıkça çıkamazsınız, firar edemezsiniz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since there is no escape from God’s dominion, the refrain asks how people dare to be ungrateful toward Him.
rows.anchor: her nereden bakılsa O’nun hükm ü saltanatı hudûdundan çıkmak imkânı olmadığı hâlde O’na karşı nasıl küfr ü küfranda bulunmaya cür’et edersiniz?

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Shuwaz” is a flame or blaze of fire sent against the two groups.
rows.anchor: salınır üstünüze ateşten bir yalın bir alev

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Nuhas” may mean molten copper, copper-colored smoke, or poisonous smoke; its flame burns and its smoke suffocates, leaving no defense.
rows.anchor: ve bir bakır yani erimiş bakır, yahut bakır gibi bir kızıl duman, yahut bir zehirli duman ki yalını yakar, dumanı boğar

rows.speaker: Bahr
rows.claim: Al-Bahr says the passage challenges jinn and humans by establishing that they cannot escape.
rows.anchor: Bahr’da der ki: “Bu ifadeden maksad cinn ü insi ta‘cîzdir. Yani kaçamayacaklarını takrirdir.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat evokes, in the author’s own time, the firepower of modern cannons and airplane bombs.
rows.anchor: Lâkin şâyân-ı dikkattir ki bu tarz-ı tehdid zamanımız toplarının, tayyare bombalarının ateşlerini andırır şekilde bir tasvir telkin etmektedir.

rows.speaker: Dahhâk
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Shayba transmits from al-Dahhak that a fire will also emerge from the west in this world and gather people, even monkeys; pigs will lie and sleep where people had done so.
rows.anchor: İbn Ebî Şeybe’nin bu âyette Dahhâk’ten tahrîcine göre, bu dünyada da olacak, mağrib tarafından bir ateş çıkacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat is a favor because it distinguishes the obedient from the disobedient; taking vengeance on unbelievers is also a favor.
rows.anchor: tehdid bir lütuf ki mutî‘ile âsîyi tefrik ve kâfirlerden intikam da bir nimettir deniliyor.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the threat and refrain may be linked as a parenthetical circumstantial clause, with an implied “it is said” before the fire is sent.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh bunları kavil takdiriyle bir cümle-i hâliye suretinde rabt da mümkindir. Yani böyle denerek ateş salınır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the onset of Resurrection, heaven splits or cracks as it is about to fold, turns fiery red like a rose, and melts like oil.
rows.anchor: yarıldı mı yani kıyamet kopmaya başlayıp gök dürülmek üzere çatladığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional “when” has an omitted answer because the ensuing terrors and upheavals cannot be understood or adequately described now.
rows.anchor: şartiye, cevâbı mahzuftur. Yani şimdi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation treats the warning of terrifying upheavals as kindness guiding people toward rescue; another takes the refrain as reproach and punishment for deniers.
rows.anchor: zira o hâileli dehşetli inkılab günlerini haber vererek halâsa irşad ve terbiye için ihtar dahi eltâf-ı ilâhiyedendir. Yahut o günler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not asking about sin does not cancel reckoning or responsibility: the guilty are not questioned to discover whether they are criminals, since they are already identified and are not confused with the innocent.
rows.anchor: ne ins ne de cânn günahından

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals are recognized by their marks and seized by their forelocks and feet, idiomatically caught by the collar and tail.
rows.anchor: perçemleriyle ayaklarından tutulur daha Türkçesi yaka paça yakalanırlar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The refrain may be spoken as criminals are seized, or their seizure may itself count as a favor to those who are not criminals.
rows.anchor: mücrimlerin bu suretle yakalanması mücrim olmayanlar için bir nimet olur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage points out that this is the very Hell the criminals used to deny.
rows.anchor: mücrimler onu tekzib ediyor, yalan diyorlardı.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned move between Hell’s fire and boiling water.
rows.anchor: onun beyniyle o cehennem ateşi ile

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Hamim” means hot water, and “ani” means water heated to the utmost degree.
rows.anchor: “Hamîm” sıcak su, “Ânî” son derece kızgın.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question marks the criminals’ punishment for their crimes, unbelief, and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: diye cürümlerinin, küfür ve küfranlarının cezâsı çektirilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After describing the manifestations of divine majesty, the discourse turns to describe the manifestations of divine generosity.
rows.anchor: Zü’l-celâli ve’l-ikrâm’ın celâl tecelliyâtı bu suretle beyan olunduktan sonra ikram tecelliyâtını beyan için de buyuruluyor ki:
